title.en: Worldview 'gulf' behind strained Australia and China ties
title.zh: 澳大利亚和中国关系紧张背后的世界观“鸿沟”

summary.en: Australia's former ambassador to China listed "diverging worldviews" as one of the many barriers to a healthy relationship.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及对脆弱群体的怜悯。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Australia is unlikely ever to have a true partnership with China due to a mismatch of worldviews, rendering it pointless to pursue that goal, the nation's former top diplomat to China says.

But in an analysis for the Lowy Institute, Australia's former ambassador to China Graham Fletcher noted several wildcards, such as Chinese military action in Taiwan, could still disrupt the "modest new normal" of the relationship.

The change in government at the 2022 federal election acted as a circuit-breaker in increasingly fraught dealings between the nations, although they had still been marred by intimidatory military encounters involving Chinese forces, he said.

China sparked widespread international condemnation over its launch of a ballistic missile into the South Pacific in July following the signing of a landmark mutual defence alliance between Australia and Fiji.

The Albanese government sought to stabilise relations with China after diplomatic tensions peaked during the COVID-19 pandemic under then-prime minister Scott Morrison's leadership.

China slapped $20 billion in trade sanctions on Australian exports, measures that have slowly been wound back.

China is Australia's largest trading partner and is the destination for about a third of the nation's exports.

Fletcher said China had not given up hope of drawing Australia closer into its orbit, while Australia was more focused on consolidating its current relationship.

"But this relationship is unlikely ever to become genuinely close — like the relaxed, intimate fellowship Australia enjoys with like-minded partners elsewhere in its region and beyond," he said.

"The gulf in terms of diverging world views and national security agendas is simply too wide.

"It would be pointless for Canberra to pursue such a goal; it recognises this and is realistic."

The "mismatch" of world views made the relationship vulnerable to disruption, with key risks including another round of serious disagreements or the cataclysm of a conflict, including the use of force against Taiwan.

"An upheaval or conflict is always a possibility, though not in my opinion a strong one at present," the former diplomat said.

Australia would be on firmer ground when facing China if policies had cross-party support and politicians did not "seek to exploit difficulties for domestic advantage", Fletcher said.

"Bipartisanship produces policy consistency and limits China's ability to play games within the Australian system," he said.

title.en: Israel rejects Trump's 15-point plan for Gaza, Netanyahu says
title.zh: 内塔尼亚胡表示，以色列拒绝特朗普针对加沙的15点计划

summary.en: Israel's PM says its military will not pull out from Gaza until Hamas is "genuinely" disarmed.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has rejected US President Donald Trump's 15-point plan for Gaza, stating that no military pull-out will happen until Hamas is "genuinely" disarmed.

Trump's Board of Peace said last month it had reached an agreement for the "complete disarmament" of Hamas and other armed groups in Gaza.

But Hamas said handing over its heavy weapons was contingent on Israel ending "all forms of aggression" and withdrawing its forces from Gaza.

Israel has continued to carry out strikes on Gaza since agreeing to an initial ceasefire in the territory last October.

"Israel rejects the 15-point document," Netanyahu said at a cabinet meeting on Sunday.

The Israeli military "will not carry out any withdrawal until Hamas is genuinely disarmed and will continue to thwart threats against our forces and our citizens", he added.

A Hamas official told the BBC on Sunday the group "reaffirms it commitment" to the agreement and it was ready "to engage seriously and responsibly in implementing" the 15-point plan.

They called on mediators to ensure "that all parties comply with what has been agreed".

Israel's rejection signals another blow for Trump's Gaza peace plan which was announced in September last year.

The plan included the creation of the Board of Peace to oversee the agreement's implementation, as well as the disarmament of Hamas, withdrawal of Israeli troops and reconstruction of Gaza.

But he has taken some time to make it, perhaps reflecting the difficult position the Israeli leader is in.

He clearly is unhappy with Trump's plan but at the same time he will not want to upset his closest ally.

It's just over a week since Trump announced what he called a "monumental step toward lasting peace and security" - that Hamas for the first time had agreed to disarm, on condition that Israel withdraws its forces from Gaza.

On Sunday, Netanyahu was clear that was not going to happen under his watch. He said Hamas had to disarm first, adding that it couldn't be some "fictitious disarmament" - it had to be real.

The reality is any disarmament and withdrawal of Israeli forces would likely need to be phased.

Netanyahu said he was now in discussion with US officials about how to go forward.

"They have ideas; some of them are acceptable to us and some are not, and we know how to stand our ground on these matters," he said.

But just months before Israeli elections and under pressure from members of his right-wing coalition to take a tough stance on Gaza, he is unlikely to want to make concessions.

He has faced calls from far-right parts of the coalition to hold a new cabinet vote and end the Gaza plan, including National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir who dismissed the draft as "not acceptable".

title.en: More than 1 million evacuated, flights cancelled, as Typhoon Dolphin hits eastern China
title.zh: 台风“海豚”袭击中国东部，逾百万人撤离，航班取消

summary.en: A powerful typhoon named Dolphin has led to the evacuation of over one million people in eastern China and caused numerous flight cancellations. The storm previously impacted Japan, resulting in six injuries and widespread power outages affecting more than 50,000 buildings.
summary.zh: 台风“海豚”袭击中国东部，导致超过一百万人撤离，航班取消。此前，该气旋已横扫日本，造成六人受伤，并导致逾五万栋建筑停电。

body.en:
The strongest tropical cyclone to hit China this year has slammed into the country’s eastern coast on Sunday, unleashing torrential rain and powerful winds.

Typhoon Dolphin had already swept across Japan’s southern Okinawa prefecture, injuring six people and cutting power to more than 50,000 buildings.

It then made landfall near Yuhuan in eastern Zhejiang province on Sunday evening, China's meteorological authorities said.

The storm packed maximum sustained winds of 151 km/h near its centre at landfall, equivalent to a Category 1 hurricane on the Saffir-Simpson scale.

Authorities had moved offshore workers to safety, ordered vessels back to port and increased checks at reservoirs, mountain streams, landslide-prone areas, construction sites and tourist locations.

Torrential rain is forecast through August 10 across Zhejiang, Shanghai, northern Fujian, northeastern Jiangxi, central and southern Anhui, and much of Jiangsu. Parts of central and eastern Zhejiang could receive 250-500 mm of rain, according to forecasters.

After landfall, Dolphin is forecast to track westward before slowing over central and southwestern China and gradually losing strength, Wang Haiping, chief forecaster at the National Meteorological Centre, told state broadcaster CCTV.

That could prolong heavy rain and raise the risk of flooding and landslides, especially in mountainous areas and along smaller rivers.

Transport was widely disrupted across the east of the country, and more than 1 million people were evacuated from their homes.

In addition to evacuating at least 30,300 people, Shanghai has cancelled about 1,500 flights, according to flight-tracking data provider VariFlight.

A 42-year-old tourist from Guangdong, surnamed Chen, said he was stranded in Shanghai after his family's flight, scheduled to depart on Sunday, was canceled due to Typhoon Dolphin.

He said the family had been rebooked on a flight at 10 pm on Monday, although they were unsure whether it would be able to take off.

"To us Guangdong people, this typhoon is as ordinary as having a meal and feeling the wind. It's just part of everyday life," Chen said, adding that the storm did not appear particularly strong by the standards of China's southern coast.

In neighbouring Zhejiang province, the city of Wenzhou relocated more than 900,000 residents and opened more than 1,000 emergency shelters.

In Fujian province, authorities evacuated 98,900 people from high-risk areas after raising the typhoon emergency response to Level 3, according to Xinhua. Zhejiang, Shanghai and Jiangsu have also activated Level 3 emergency responses.

title.en: Suspected crime boss Daniel Kinahan appears in court after extradition

summary.en: The Irish Prison Service bought a bulletproof and bombproof van to transport the 49-year-old to court after his extradition from Dubai.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及公义、尊严与问责。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Suspected crime boss Daniel Kinahan, one of the world's most wanted men, has appeared before a Dublin court after being extradited from Dubai.

He has been charged with directing the activities of a criminal organisation between 18 October 2015 and 6 April 2017.

An Irish government jet carrying the 49-year-old landed in Dublin after 18:00 local time. He was arrested and charged upon his arrival.

Following a 13-minute non-jury hearing at the Special Criminal Court, he was remanded in custody until 5 October.

Kinahan was arrested in the United Arab Emirates (UAE) in April. He appealed the extradition order over the past few months but his attempts were unsuccessful.

The National Crime Agency (NCA) has previously said that the Kinahan cartel has been responsible for importing tonnes of drugs and firearms around the world and has also been linked to more than a dozen gangland murders.

Kinahan was not only wanted by the authorities in Ireland - the US Treasury Department once described the Kinahan cartel as one of the most dangerous in the world.

The US government imposed sanctions on Kinahan in April 2022 after identifying him and other member of his family as leaders of the Kinahan organised crime cartel.

He fought attempts to extradite him back to his native country, where the Kinahan cartel was involved in a long-running gangland feud that claimed 18 lives.

Ahead of the extradition, the Irish Prison Service bought a bulletproof and bombproof van which can be used to escort prisoners who are considered high-risk.

Garda Commissioner Justin Kelly said the arrest shows the force's determination to "target transnational organised crime groups" alongside international policing partners such as Dubai police.

He added it shows the value of the force's relationship with the authorities in the UAE, the Irish ministry of justice at judicial level, and "on a police-to-police basis".

Kinahan arrived at Baldonnell Casement Aerodrome on Sunday evening, where gardaí arrested and charged him.

He was directly transported under heavy police guard to the Criminal Courts of Justice in Dublin.

All the benches were full in a packed courtroom of journalists, a number of solicitors from the Director of Public Prosecutions (DPP), some members of the public and court clerks.

He appeared before judges Patrick McGrath, Sarah Berkeley and Fiona Lydon, and rose to his feet when the three judges took their places.

Kinahan did not have legal representation, and told the court that he did not have time to arrange this.

When Judge McGrath suggested that he should be charged today and legal representation arranged later on, Kinahan replied: "If I have time, yes."

Netanyahu said Israel would not accept the proposal, which links Hamas's disarmament to an eventual Israeli military withdrawal, in its current form.

"Israel does not accept the 15-point document," Netanyahu said during a cabinet meeting in Jerusalem on Sunday.

Netanyahu said this applied to all weapons, not just heavy weapons. The prime minister also reaffirmed his opposition to an independent Palestinian state.

Hamas made the surrender of heavy weapons conditional on several requirements, including the withdrawal of Israeli forces from the Gaza Strip and the establishment of a Palestinian state.

As part of a peace plan brokered by US President Donald Trump, an internationally staffed Board of Peace was established at the beginning of the year.

title.en: Nigerian army says it safely rescued 33 people kidnapped by gunmen
title.zh: 尼日利亚军队称安全解救了33名被武装分子绑架的人员

summary.en: The Nigerian army announced the safe rescue of 33 individuals who had been abducted by gunmen while traveling through Zamfara state on Saturday.
summary.zh: 尼日利亚军方宣布，33名周六在扎姆法拉州旅行时被武装分子绑架的人员已安全获救。

body.en:
Nigeria's army has said it safely rescued 33 people after they were kidnapped by armed men while travelling through the country's north-western Zamfara state.

The army said its troops mobilised alongside the police immediately after hearing about the abduction, in the Tsafe area of Zamfara on Saturday afternoon.

The military found the kidnappers in the process of moving the hostages to an unknown location, the army said, and the gunmen fled into the nearby bush after coming under fire.

Kidnappings by armed groups who hold people for ransom are common in parts of north-western Nigeria and major roads have become targets for attacks.

Analysts say ransom payments by desperate families, intermediaries or, in some cases, Nigerian authorities have fuelled the abductions.

Nigerian army spokesman Lt-Col Aliyu Danja said it was unclear where the abductors were moving their hostages when troops intercepted them, adding that the army was now attempting to track the kidnappers.

"The troops engaged the terrorists with effective fire, forcing them to abandon the victims and flee into adjoining bushes," he said, noting that all the hostages had been recovered without any casualties.

Danja warned members of the public in the region to remain vigilant and pass on relevant information to security forces.

Nigeria's security forces have recorded a recent success in rescuing kidnapped victims.

On Thursday, the country's presidency said that more than 300 people abducted in separate attacks in Nigeria had been rescued.

Those freed included 163 people abducted in an attack in February on the Woro and Nuku communities in Kwara state, where scores were killed. At least 145 others had been taken in Niger state.

The rescue came weeks after 44 pupils and teachers abducted during a raid on a school in Oyo state were freed after more than 50 days in captivity.

Nigeria's President Bola Tinubu said on Wednesday that soldiers would get a pay increase of up to 80% for the government's "deep appreciation" of those battling the nation's enormous security threats.

Tinubu is attempting to curb widespread banditry, kidnappings and violence from various armed groups, including Islamist militants.

Continuing insecurity nationwide has become a major political issue ahead of the 2027 elections.
body.zh: 尼日利亚军队表示，33 名在穿越该国西北部扎姆法拉州时被武装人员绑架的人被安全救出。 军方表示，周六下午在扎姆法拉的特安全地区发生绑架事件后，军队立即与警方一起动员起来。 军方表示，绑匪是在将人质转移到不明地点的过程中发现的，枪手在遭到枪击后逃进了附近的灌木丛。 武装团体绑架勒索的事件在尼日利亚西北部部分地区很常见，主要道路已成为袭击目标。 分析人士表示，绝望的家庭、中间人或在某些情况下尼日利亚当局支付的赎金助长了绑架事件。 尼日利亚陆军发言人阿利尤·丹贾中校表示，目前尚不清楚绑架者在军队拦截人质时正在将人质转移到哪里，并补充说，军队目前正在试图追踪绑架者。 他说：“部队以有效火力与恐怖分子交战，迫使他们抛弃受害者并逃入邻近的灌木丛。”他指出，所有人质均已被救出，没有造成任何人员伤亡。 丹贾警告该地区公众保持警惕，并将相关信息传递给安全部队。 尼日利亚安全部队最近在营救被绑架受害者方面取得了成功。 周四，该国总统表示，在尼日利亚多起袭击事件中被绑架的 300 多人已获救。 被释放的人包括 2 月份夸拉州沃罗和努库社区袭击中被绑架的 163 人，数十人被杀。尼日尔州至少还有 145 人被带走。 几周前，奥约州一所学校遭到袭击时被绑架的 44 名学生和教师在被关押 50 多天后获释。 尼日利亚总统博拉·蒂努布周三表示，由于政府对那些与国家巨大安全威胁作斗争的人们的“深切赞赏”，士兵们的工资将增加高达 80%。 蒂努布正试图遏制包括伊斯兰武装分子在内的各种武装团体普遍存在的土匪、绑架和暴力行为。 全国范围内持续的不安全局势已成为 2027 年选举之前的一个重大政治问题。

title.en: Man arrested after boat capsizes near Statue of Liberty killing woman and infant
title.zh: 自由女神像附近船只倾覆致一女子和一名婴儿死亡，一名男子被捕

summary.en: A Good Samaritan vessel rescued 12 people from the water before police arrived, the US Coast Guard says.
summary.zh: 美国海岸警卫队称，在警方抵达前，一艘“好撒玛利亚人”船只从水中救起了12人。

body.en:
The operator of a boat that overturned near the Statue of Liberty, killing a woman and a baby, has been arrested and charged with reckless endangerment, New York police said.

Officials said a large search and rescue operation was launched after the incident near New York Harbour on Saturday night. Twelve people who were initially rescued from the water are all reported to be in stable condition.

New York police divers later found a 27-year-old woman and a five-month-old girl, who were transported to a nearby hospital where they later died.

The names of passengers and the specific cause of the incident have not been released by officials.

Around 22:25 local time (03:25 BST), police received a 911 call reporting an overturned boat in the waters near Liberty Island, which houses the iconic statue.

A nearby tour operator Sea the City saw the capsized boat and helped pull 11 people from the water, the company's founder Adam Schwartz said according to the BBC's US partner CBS News.

The rescue involved two Coast Guard boats, four fire department boats, two police boats and a police helicopter, the USCG said.

The boat's operator, a 46-year-old Manhattan resident, faces 13 counts of reckless endangerment, officials said.

Coast Guard investigators are also determining whether the boat was illegally chartered.

An illegal charter is any passenger-for-hire vessel operation that does not have required credentials, safety equipment, and certificate of inspection.

"We are extremely grateful for the heroic, swift actions of our partner agencies and Good Samaritan vessel who assisted in rescuing survivors from the water," said Capt Doreen McCarthy of the USCG.
body.zh: 纽约警方称，一艘在自由女神像附近翻船并造成一名妇女和婴儿死亡的船只的操作者已被捕，并被指控鲁莽危害他人安全。 官员们表示，周六晚纽约港附近发生事件后，展开了大规模搜救行动。 海岸警卫队称，在警察到达之前，一艘好撒玛利亚人的船只从水中救出了 12 人。纽约警方潜水员后来发现了一名 27 岁的妇女和一名 5 个月大的女孩，她们被送往附近的一家医院，后来不治身亡。 乘客姓名和事件具体原因尚未公布。 当地时间 22:25 左右（英国夏令时 03:25），警方接到 911 电话，报告称自由岛附近海域有一艘船翻倒，该岛坐落着标志性雕像。 美国海岸警卫队表示，救援行动涉及两艘海岸警卫队船只、四艘消防船、两艘警船和一架警用直升机。 官员表示，对该事件的调查正在进行中。官员称，该船的经营者是一名 46 岁的曼哈顿居民，他面临 13 项鲁莽危害他人安全的罪名。 海岸警卫队调查人员还在确定这艘船是否是非法包租的。 海岸警卫队上尉多琳·麦卡锡 (Doreen McCarthy) 表示：“我们非常感谢我们的合作伙伴机构和好撒玛利亚人船只所采取的英勇而迅速的行动，他们协助营救了水中的幸存者。”

reflection.en: In the wake of a tragic accident, the swift action of a 'Good Samaritan' vessel reminds us of the profound call to be a neighbor to those in distress. Yahweh's word challenges us to consider who truly acts as a neighbor, extending compassion and aid without hesitation.

title.en: The subtle policy shift in Tokyo that has Nagasaki sounding the alarm
title.zh: 东京微妙的政策转变让长崎敲响警钟

summary.en: Nagasaki's mayor has voiced strong opposition to nuclear weapons, labeling them an "absolute evil," amidst reports that Tokyo is reconsidering its long-held non-nuclear principles.
summary.zh: 长崎市市长强烈反对核武器，称其为“绝对邪恶”，此前有报道称东京正在重新考虑其长期坚持的无核原则。

body.en:
The Japanese city of Nagasaki has used the 81st anniversary of the atomic bombing to call for the abolition of nuclear weapons while criticising countries that use them as a deterrent.

"Nuclear weapons are not a necessary evil but an absolute evil, and can never coexist with humanity," Mayor Shiro Suzuki said in a speech broadcast by Japanese public television channel NHK.

The mayor also asked the Japanese government to maintain the "three non-nuclear principles," adopted as a resolution by the Japanese parliament in 1971 but never incorporated into Japanese law: not to possess, not to produce, and not to allow nuclear weapons to be brought into the country.

At the same ceremony, Japan's new right-wing leader, Sanae Takaichi said her government defended the three principles without clarifying whether the country would continue to respect them in the future.

She said the government would defend realistic and practical measures to achieve a world free of nuclear weapons.

The anniversary passes as the Japanese government prepares to review its key national security documents, raising questions about whether the nuclear principles will remain intact.

Questions around Japan's nuclear weapons policy have been raised after Defence Minister Shinjiro Koizumi recently called for a "taboo-free" national debate on the subject.

The long-standing anti-nuclear stance is increasingly under pressure as East Asian neighbours — notably China — boost their military capabilities, while doubts persist about the reliability of Tokyo's biggest security backer, the United States.

The prime minister has already lifted Japan's self-imposed ban on weapons exports and expanded defence spending, while pushing to amend the constitution.

Those policies have drawn rebukes from China, which accuses Japan of "new militarism" and Takaichi of bending to the whims of the far right.

In December, an unnamed senior administration official told local media in an off-the-record session suggesting that Japan should possess nuclear weapons.

The remark was widely reported by major Japanese outlets including national broadcaster NHK and Asahi Shimbun, sparking public criticism.

"If I look at it cynically, I can't help but think that maybe she really wants to change" Japan's anti-nuclear commitment, 82-year-old Satoshi Tanaka, a campaigner who survived the 1945 attack on Hiroshima, told the Agence-France Presse news agency.

Sunday's ceremony in Nagasaki included a message from United Nations Secretary-General Antonio Guterres, who made a strong anti-war plea and a case for diplomacy.

title.en: Australia: Jetstar, Qatar Airways planes almost collide on Sydney Airport tarmac
title.zh: 澳大利亚：捷星航空和卡塔尔航空飞机在悉尼机场停机坪险些相撞

summary.en: A flight crew member was injured in a near-miss collision between two planes on the tarmac at Sydney Airport in Australia. An investigation has been launched to determine the cause of the incident.
summary.zh: 在澳大利亚悉尼机场的停机坪上，两架飞机险些相撞，一名机组人员受伤。目前已启动调查，以确定事故原因。

body.en:
A flight crew member was injured in a near-miss collision on the runway at Australia's Sydney Airport. An investigation has been launched to determine what caused the incident.

Two passenger aircraft —  a Jetstar and a Qatar Airways plane —  came close to crashing into each other on the tarmac at Australia's   busiest Sydney Airport on Sunday.

A crew member was injured and the incident has triggered a probe by the country's safety regulators.

The Jetstar A320 was taxiing for takeoff to the Gold Coast in the state of Queensland when its flight crew saw the Qatar Airways Boeing 777 —  which was being towed by an aircraft tug —  in close proximity on a crossing taxiway, the Australian Transport Safety Bureau (ATSB) said in a statement.

"Both aircraft were stopped abruptly", the statement said, leading to a Jestar cabin crew member moving through the cabin being injured and the connection between the 777 nose gear and aircraft tug suffering damage.

The ATSB said that investigators were gathering data from both the planes, air traffic control, and interviewing crew and tug operators to determine the cause of the near collision.

The regulator put out a call for witnesses at the airport to send in any visuals of the incident.

Jetstar —  which is a low-cost subsidiary of  Australia's national carrier Qantas — said it was also conducting its own investigation.

"Our aircraft was following ⁠instructions ​by Air Traffic Control when the ​pilots were forced to brake firmly after another aircraft came in ​close proximity," a ‌Jetstar spokesperson said.

There was no immediate statement from Qatar Airways, which is the flag carrier of Qatar.

Meanwhile, flights at Sydney Airport were experiencing delays following the incident, government agency Airservices Australia said.

Sunday's incident ⁠comes a day after Sydney Airport witnessed widespread delays ⁠sparked by Airservices Australia authorizing  "departure spacing" due to roster issues with air traffic controllers.

title.en: First day in office: Colombia's new president faces deadly bombings
title.zh: 上任首日：哥伦比亚新总统面临致命炸弹袭击

summary.en: Colombia's new President Abelardo De la Espriella began his term with two deadly bombings, leading him to promise a relentless anti-terror crackdown.
summary.zh: 哥伦比亚新任总统阿韦拉多·德拉埃斯普列拉上任首日即遭遇两起致命炸弹袭击，他誓言将展开无情的反恐打击。

body.en:
Two bombing attacks in different parts of Colombia on Saturday marred the first day in office for new President Abelardo de la Espriella, leaving at least one police officer dead and several wounded.

The tough-talking hard-right leader campaigned on confronting "narcoterrorism without truce" and ending peace talks with armed groups following his inauguration on Saturday in the southwestern city of Cali.

Colombia's army said FARC guerrilla dissidents used explosives to destroy a highway tollbooth near Cali in the early hours of Saturday, with two security guards suffering minor injuries.

Rebels under the command of Ivan Morodisco, Colombia's most wanted guerrilla commander, operate in the area surrounding the tollbooth, which was under construction on the Pan-American highway in the Santander de Quilichao municipality.

Morodisco leads dissidents who broke away from the historic 2016 peace agreement between the FARC and Colombia's government.

De la Espriella condemned the bombing on social media, saying "attacking the country's infrastructure is attacking progress".

"To those responsible, I send a clear message: there will be no refuge, no leniency and no impunity," he added.

About 1,000 kilometers away, in the northern department of Cesar, an officer was killed in another bombing early Sunday when an explosive-equipped drone struck a police station, officials there said.

Authorities there have not yet identified suspects, but De la Espriella vowed whoever is responsible "will not go unpunished."

The confrontational style of the first-time political leader, who openly admires US President Donald Trump and El Salvador's hardline Nayib Bukele, now faces tough opposition from the guerrilla groups and drug traffickers operating in Colombia.

De la Espriella has promised to open mega-prisons like Bukele and to intensify bombing raids against guerrilla groups and drug traffickers operating in Colombia, with support from the United States and Israel.

His inauguration comes during the worst wave of violence the country has experienced in the last decade.

A decade after landmark peace accords, pockets of Colombia are still ruled by dissident armed groups that dominate global cocaine production.

Roberto Sandoval, a firefighter who lives in the neighborhood next to the tollbooth, told the Agence France-Presse news agency that tensions were high following the bombing.

Elsewhere in the neighborhood, the blast shattered windows and left glass strewn on the bed of Sonia Zapata, a 68-year-old housewife.

The US State Department announced on Saturday that Trump plans to provide US $1 billion ($1.4B) in security...

title.en: Nigeria marries 1,500 couples in mass wedding
title.zh: 尼日利亚举行千人集体婚礼

summary.en: Nigerian authorities organized a mass wedding for 1,500 couples, stating the initiative aims to support low-income families and enhance social stability. The program included individuals who had experienced the loss of family members due to violent attacks.
summary.zh: 尼日利亚政府为1,500对新人举行了集体婚礼，称此举旨在支持低收入家庭并促进社会稳定。参与婚礼的人群中，包括那些在暴力袭击中失去亲人的家庭成员。

body.en:
The government describes the program as a way to support low-income families and promote social stability. Among those married were people who lost family members in violent attacks.

Some 1,500 couples got married at a mass wedding organized by Abba Kabir Yusuf, the governor of Kano state, in northern Nigeria .

The regional government described the two-day event as a way to support low-income families and promote social stability.

"The whole idea for the marriage is to help our families and we husbands who are not financially stable to marry; that's why the government is helping us get married," groom Abubakar Aliyu Musa told the Associated Press.

According to Kano's regional government, each bride received a dowry of 200,000 naira ($147, €127) and support to set up a small business.

The couples were also given household items including beds, mattresses and blankets.

Governor Yusuf described the program as a "bold social intervention aimed at restoring hope and supporting dignified family life in Kano."

"The program was designed not only to assist women who might otherwise struggle to afford marriage, but also to strengthen families and promote social stability in the state," he said.

Among those who participated in the mass wedding were people who lost family members in violent attacks.

One of them was Haruna Bashir, who lost his wife and six children in an attack earlier in the year. Daurawa hailed the ceremony as a step toward Bashir "gradually returning to normal life" after having "hardly interacted with people … since the tragic incident."

Nigeria has been grappling with a major security crisis for years, particularly in the country's north, which is regularly hit by raids and attacks by Islamist insurgents and organized gangs.

Many armed groups in Nigeria also kidnap schoolchildren to demand large ransoms.

On Wednesday, the Nigerian government announced the release of 308 people who had been abducted.

title.en: Kosovo PM Kurti egged in parliament amid political crisis
title.zh: 科索沃总理库尔蒂在政治危机中怂恿议会

summary.en: Kosovo has held three elections in over two years. Albin Kurti's ruling Vetevendosje is struggling to garner the two-thirds majority required to elect a president.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及领导、智慧与公共责任。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Kosovo has held three elections in over two years. Albin Kurti's ruling Vetevendosje is struggling to garner the two-thirds majority required to elect a president.

Kosovo's parliament was suspended on Saturday after an opposition lawmaker threw eggs at caretaker Prime Minister Albin Kurti .

"Shame on you!" Time Kadrijaj of the conservative opposition Alliance for the Future of Kosovo (AAK) party shouted in parliament before hurling eggs at Kurti.

In response, Kurti said that he was "happy to pay this price" if it was the cost of dialogue.

Kurti's left-wing Vetevendosje (VV) party is known for its own parliamentary disruptions, with party representatives launching tear gas in the chamber in 2018 and also on multiple occasions in 2015.

The incident comes after days of negotiations as Kurti attempts to gain enough opposition support to elect a new president amid Kosovo's broader political crisis.

Kurti achieved his parliamentary majority with ethnic minority MPs in a December election that followed an inconclusive vote in February 2025.

His VV party's share of the vote fell from 51% to 43% in a snap election in June, but it maintained a parliamentary majority alongside ethnic minority allies.

However, Kurti requires a two-thirds majority in parliament to elect a president.

The current negotiations seem to have ground to another stalemate, with neither side having agreed to a candidate.

A constitutional deadline to elect a speaker of parliament expired on Friday. Opposition lawmakers have threatened legal action over Kurti's request for more time to negotiate.

Kosovo declared independence from Serbia in 2008 after the 1998-99 war, which ended with Serbia's withdrawal following a NATO bombing campaign.

Kosovo has been recognized by over half of the world's countries , including the United States and most European Union countries.

title.en: War, terror, diplomacy: What if Israel takes Al-Aqsa Mosque?
title.zh: 战争、恐怖、外交：如果以色列占领阿克萨清真寺会怎样？

summary.en: Reports from Jerusalem indicate that Israeli authorities may be taking control of the Al-Aqsa Mosque, a highly sacred Islamic site. Experts warn that such an action could trigger severe repercussions, including war, terrorism, and the termination of diplomatic relations.
summary.zh: 来自耶路撒冷的报道称，以色列当局可能正在接管伊斯兰教最神圣的地点之一——阿克萨清真寺。专家警告说，如果发生这种情况，可能会引发严重后果，包括战争、恐怖主义以及外交关系的终结。

body.en:
Reports from Jerusalem suggest that Israeli authorities are taking over one of Islam's holiest sites, the Al-Aqsa Mosque. If they do, experts say anything could happen, from war to terrorism to ending diplomatic ties.

The statement issued after this week's meeting in Jordan was blunt about what might happen next.

Israeli infringements on one of Islam's holiest sites, the Al-Aqsa Mosque in east Jerusalem, could lead to "a religious conflict with repercussions that will extend beyond the region and threaten regional and international peace and security," the foreign ministers of 10 countries belonging to the Arab League said after Wednesday's emergency meeting  in Amman, Jordan. The statement was also signed by ministers from Indonesia, Pakistan, Turkey, and Malaysia.

Jordan's foreign minister called the meeting because of mounting evidence that the Israeli government is surreptitiously changing a decades-old agreement meant to ensure intercommunal peace at the Al-Aqsa Mosque compound, an area of great religious significance to Muslims, Jews, and Christians.

"We warn that tampering with the status quo … could trigger a religious conflict that will reverberate beyond Palestine and Jordan into the whole Muslim world," Foreign Minister Ayman Safadi told the UK newspaper  the Guardian  before the meeting.

Israel's Foreign Ministry issued a response, saying the statement was inaccurate and  Jerusalem "has never been more open and accessible to worshippers of all faiths."

Al-Aqsa is considered the third-holiest site in Islam , after Mecca and Medina in Saudi Arabia. The compound, also known as the Temple Mount, is also Judaism 's holiest site — two Jewish temples are thought to have stood there — and it is also of significance to Christians for its biblical connections to Jesus Christ's life.

Al-Aqsa also bears a lot of political weight because the mosque is seen by many as the embodiment of Palestinian identity, a flashpoint in a city sought as the capital of any eventual Palestinian state .

Because of the site's importance, when Israel first occupied East Jerusalem in 1967, it was deemed in the interests of Israeli national security to keep allowing Muslims to worship there. summary.en: Australia's former ambassador to China listed "diverging worldviews" as one of the many barriers to a healthy relationship.

body.en:
Australia is unlikely ever to have a true partnership with China due to a mismatch of worldviews, rendering it pointless to pursue that goal, the nation's former top diplomat to China says.

But in an analysis for the Lowy Institute, Australia's former ambassador to China Graham Fletcher noted several wildcards, such as Chinese military action in Taiwan, could still disrupt the "modest new normal" of the relationship.

The change in government at the 2022 federal election acted as a circuit-breaker in increasingly fraught dealings between the nations, although they had still been marred by intimidatory military encounters involving Chinese forces, he said.

China sparked widespread international condemnation over its launch of a ballistic missile into the South Pacific in July following the signing of a landmark mutual defence alliance between Australia and Fiji.

The Albanese government sought to stabilise relations with China after diplomatic tensions peaked during the COVID-19 pandemic under then-prime minister Scott Morrison's leadership.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

China slapped $20 billion in trade sanctions on Australian exports, measures that have slowly been wound back.

China is Australia's largest trading partner and is the destination for about a third of the nation's exports.

Fletcher said China had not given up hope of drawing Australia closer into its orbit, while Australia was more focused on consolidating its current relationship.

"But this relationship is unlikely ever to become genuinely close — like the relaxed, intimate fellowship Australia enjoys with like-minded partners elsewhere in its region and beyond," he said.

"The gulf in terms of diverging world views and national security agendas is simply too wide.

"It would be pointless for Canberra to pursue such a goal; it recognises this and is realistic."

The "mismatch" of world views made the relationship vulnerable to disruption, with key risks including another round of serious disagreements or the cataclysm of a conflict, including the use of force against Taiwan.

"An upheaval or conflict is always a possibility, though not in my opinion a strong one at present," the former diplomat said.

Australia would be on firmer ground when facing China if policies had cross-party support and politicians did not "seek to exploit difficulties for domestic advantage", Fletcher said.

"Bipartisanship produces policy consistency and limits China's ability to play games within the Australian system," he said.

title.en: More than 1 million evacuated, flights cancelled, as Typhoon Dolphin hits eastern China

summary.en: The cyclone had already swept across Japan, injuring six people and cutting power to more than 50,000 buildings.

body.en:
The strongest tropical cyclone to hit China this year has slammed into the country’s eastern coast on Sunday, unleashing torrential rain and powerful winds.

Typhoon Dolphin had already swept across Japan’s southern Okinawa prefecture, injuring six people and cutting power to more than 50,000 buildings.

It then made landfall near Yuhuan in eastern Zhejiang province on Sunday evening, China's meteorological authorities said.

The storm packed maximum sustained winds of 151 km/h near its centre at landfall, equivalent to a Category 1 hurricane on the Saffir-Simpson scale.

Authorities had moved offshore workers to safety, ordered vessels back to port and increased checks at reservoirs, mountain streams, landslide-prone areas, construction sites and tourist locations.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

Torrential rain is forecast through August 10 across Zhejiang, Shanghai, northern Fujian, northeastern Jiangxi, central and southern Anhui, and much of Jiangsu. Parts of central and eastern Zhejiang could receive 250-500 mm of rain, according to forecasters.

After landfall, Dolphin is forecast to track westward before slowing over central and southwestern China and gradually losing strength, Wang Haiping, chief forecaster at the National Meteorological Centre, told state broadcaster CCTV.

That could prolong heavy rain and raise the risk of flooding and landslides, especially in mountainous areas and along smaller rivers.

Transport was widely disrupted across the east of the country, and more than 1 million people were evacuated from their homes.

In addition to evacuating at least 30,300 people, Shanghai has cancelled about 1,500 flights, according to flight-tracking data provider VariFlight.

A 42-year-old tourist from Guangdong, surnamed Chen, said he was stranded in Shanghai after his family's flight, scheduled to depart on Sunday, was canceled due to Typhoon Dolphin.

He said the family had been rebooked on a flight at 10 pm on Monday, although they were unsure whether it would be able to take off.

"To us Guangdong people, this typhoon is as ordinary as having a meal and feeling the wind. It's just part of everyday life," Chen said, adding that the storm did not appear particularly strong by the standards of China's southern coast.

In neighbouring Zhejiang province, the city of Wenzhou relocated more than 900,000 residents and opened more than 1,000 emergency shelters.

In Fujian province, authorities evacuated 98,900 people from high-risk areas after raising the typhoon emergency response to Level 3, according to Xinhua. Zhejiang, Shanghai and Jiangsu have also activated Level 3 emergency responses.

verse.textEn: Whatever you do, work at it with all your heart, as working for Yahweh, not for human masters.
verse.textZh: 无论做什么，都要从心里做，像是给主做的，不是给人做的。

title.en: Typhoon Dolphin batters Japan's Okinawa before bearing down on China
title.zh: 台风海豚袭击日本冲绳，随后逼近中国

summary.en: The storm has cut power to at least 44,000 buildings and injured five people on the Japanese island.
summary.zh: 这场风暴已导致日本岛上至少44,000栋建筑断电，并造成五人受伤。

body.en:
Typhoon Dolphin has cut power to at least 44,000 buildings and injured at least five people after hitting Japan's Okinawa island on Saturday.

Flights to and from Okinawa's main airport - Naha International Airport - were cancelled as it closed on Friday as the storm arrived.

The storm had maximum wind speeds of 162km/h (101mph) on Saturday and has been categorised as a "very strong" typhoon by the Japan Meteorological Agency, which warned of high waves, storm surges and lightning strikes.

Dolphin is expected to make landfall on China's eastern coast late on Sunday or early on Monday. Authorities there have shut ports and schools ahead of its arrival.

The main areas in Japan affected by the typhoon are the islands of Okinawa and Amami in the far south-west of the country.

Five elderly people suffered non-life-threatening injuries, according to the Okinawan prefectural government. Three of them fell because of the strong winds, it said.

Japan's national broadcaster NHK reports numerous accounts of trees being toppled by strong winds throughout Nago city in Okinawa, while a car was found overturned and leaking oil in a parking lot.

In China, Zhejiang's Ningbo Lishe International Airport said it would stop its operations from 23:30 local time on Saturday (15:30 GMT) and suspend all flights on Sunday.

A coastal typhoon alert in Zhejiang has been raised to its highest level, and port and ferry services have been halted in the Chinese province.

In Hong Kong, its weather observatory posted a record high temperature of 36.9C on Sunday as Typhoon Dolphin swept warm air over the city.

Typhoon season in the western Pacific typically occurs between May and October, when typhoons are considered more commonplace. This year is a strong El Niño year , which experts say means typhoons can grow to be more intense.

In an average year of 25 cyclones reaching tropical storm strength in the region, around three usually make landfall in Japan, according to the country's meteorological agency.

Some of these will be strong enough to be classified as typhoons – as was the case with Dolphin.

A typhoon is the term used for storms that form in the north-west Pacific, whereas a hurricane is the term used for storms that form in the Atlantic or eastern Pacific.
body.zh: 周六，台风“海豚”袭击日本冲绳岛后，已导致至少 44,000 座建筑物断电，并造成至少 5 人受伤。 由于风暴到来，冲绳主要机场那霸国际机场周五关闭，往返航班被取消。 周六，这场风暴的最大风速为 162 公里/小时（101 英里/小时），日本气象厅将其归类为“非常强”台风，并警告称会有巨浪、风暴潮和雷击。 预计海豚将于周日晚些时候或周一早些时候登陆中国东部沿海。那里的当局在其抵达前关闭了港口和学校。 日本受台风影响的主要地区是该国西南部的冲绳岛和奄美岛。 冲绳县政府称，五名老人受伤，没有生命危险。据称，其中三人因强风而倒下。 日本国家广播公司NHK报道称，冲绳名护市多处树木被强风吹倒，停车场内发现一辆汽车翻倒并漏油。 在中国，浙江宁波栎社国际机场表示将从当地时间周六23:30（格林威治标准时间15:30）开始停止运营，并于周日暂停所有航班。 浙江沿海台风警报已提升至最高级别，该省的港口和渡轮服务已停止。 西太平洋的台风季节通常发生在五月至十月之间，此时台风更为常见。今年是厄尔尼诺现象强烈的一年，专家表示，这意味着台风可能会变得更加强烈。 据日本气象厅称，该地区平均每年有 25 个达到热带风暴强度的气旋，其中约 3 个通常会在日本登陆。 其中一些强度足以被归类为台风——就像海豚的情况一样。 台风是在西北太平洋形成的风暴的术语，而飓风是在大西洋或东太平洋形成的风暴的术语。

reflection.en: As Typhoon Dolphin brings disruption and injury, communities face the immediate challenges of recovery. In such moments of hardship, Yahweh's word reminds us that suffering, when endured, can forge resilience and a deeper hope within us and our communities.
reflection.zh: 当台风海豚带来破坏和人员受伤时，社区面临着即时的恢复挑战。在这样的艰难时刻，雅伟的话语提醒我们，苦难若能忍受，便能在我们和我们的社区中锻造出韧性与更深的盼望。

verse.textEn: We also glory in our sufferings, because we know that suffering produces perseverance; perseverance, character; and character, hope.
verse.textZh: 就是在患难中也是欢欢喜喜的；因为知道患难生忍耐，忍耐生老练，老练生盼望。

title.en: President Xi never wastes a good crisis. As Iran, Ukraine and Palestine distract the world, he tightens his grip | Simon Tisdall
title.zh: 习近平主席从不浪费一场好危机。当伊朗、乌克兰和巴勒斯坦分散世界注意力时，他正在收紧控制 | 西蒙·蒂斯代尔

summary.en: The article suggests that Chinese President Xi Jinping is leveraging global distractions, such as conflicts in Iran, Ukraine, and Palestine, to consolidate power both domestically and internationally. This strategy is seen as detrimental to global order and particularly impacts minority groups within China.
summary.zh: 文章指出，中国国家主席习近平正利用伊朗、乌克兰和巴勒斯坦等全球冲突分散注意力的时机，在国内和国际上巩固权力。这种策略被认为对全球秩序有害，并特别影响到中国境内的少数民族群体。

body.en: Ever the strategist, the Chinese leader is taking the offensive, both abroad and at home. That’s bad news for global order, and minorities in his country Imagine what would happen if a British prime minister in London told the Scots they could not have their own parliament, national football team or fly the saltire. Or if the Welsh were told their language and poetry were banned and must no longer be taught in schools. The ensuing uproar would probably destroy the United Kingdom. Yet that’s exactly what Xi Jinping, China’s communist emperor, is telling the roughly 125 million members of the 55 ethnic and religious minorities who together comprise about 9% of the country’s (majority Han Chinese) population. Xi claims his sinicisation policy, embodied in a new “ethnic unity” law, will boost national identity and integration and, by expanding compulsory use of the Mandarin language, improve life and work prospects. Minorities should “hug tightly like pomegranate seeds” to build a strong, united China, he says. But Tibetans, Mongolians, Uyghurs and others who value their separate language and customs fiercely object to what they see as forced assimilation into a conformist, intolerant monoculture dominated by the Communist party’s tunnel vision. For them, it’s ethnic cleansing by another name. Simon Tisdall is a Guardian foreign affairs commentator Continue reading...

title.en: Typhoon Dolphin hits Japan as China braces for coming storm
title.zh: 台风“海豚”袭击日本，中国严阵以待

summary.en: A typhoon has struck southern Japan, causing injuries and power outages, and is now moving towards China, prompting port closures in preparation.
summary.zh: 台风“海豚”袭击日本南部，造成人员受伤和停电，目前正向中国逼近，中国已关闭港口进行防范。

body.en:
A typhoon is lashing Japan's south, causing injuries and blackouts. It is now headed for China, where ports have been closed in preparation.

Typhoon Dolphin raged over Japan 's southern regions on Saturday, causing some injuries and blackouts.

Okinawa and Amami island in Kagoshima prefecture were the areas expected to be worst affected.

The storm is expected to move on to China , making landfall along its eastern and southern ‌coast between late Sunday and early Monday, with Chinese authorities shutting down ports and ferry services ahead of the storm.

The China National Meteorological Centre Typhoon Dolphin has said Typhoon Dolphin will probably make landfall between the city of Zhoushan in Zhejiang province and the city of Fuding in Fujian province.

Zhejiang has raised its coastal typhoon alert to its highest level, while ceasing port operations and suspending 162 passenger ferry routes.

The storm is expected to bring rain and strong winds to eastern China, including parts of Shanghai, through August 12.

Some parts of eastern Zhejiang could be in for a deluge, forecasters say, with more than 600 mm (23.6 inches) of rain possible.

Ningbo ⁠Lishe ​International Airport in Zhejiang said it will stop its operations from 11:30 ​p.m. (1530 GMT) on Saturday and suspend all flights on Sunday.  

Taiwan , where 63 international flights have been cancelled, is also expected to experience heavy rain in the north over the weekend.

New political friction between Taiwan and China has also arisen after Beijing ordered that ships passing through ⁠the Taiwan Strait must heed ​its traffic control instructions amid the typhoon.

Taipei has slammed Beijing's injunctions as "ridiculous," saying that Beijing has no right to restrict access to international waters.

"The unreasonable and crude statement ‌by ​the relevant Chinese Communist departments reflects an ignorance, disregard, and trampling of international order and norms. It is utterly ridiculous!" Taiwan's Mainland Affairs Council said in a statement late ​on Friday.

China regards the democratically governed island as a breakaway territory of its own and also claims to own the strategic strait, a stance rejected by both Taipei and Washington.

title.en: School-bus-sized SpaceX rocket chunk crashes into Moon
title.zh: 校车大小的SpaceX火箭残骸坠毁月球

summary.en: A school-bus-sized chunk of a SpaceX rocket has crashed into the Moon, raising concerns among experts about increasing lunar debris. This incident occurs amidst a growing space race between the United States and China to send humans back to the Moon.
summary.zh: 一块校车大小的SpaceX火箭残骸坠毁在月球上，引发专家对月球垃圾日益增多的担忧。此事发生在中美两国竞相将人类送回月球之际。

body.en:
A piece of a SpaceX rocket that has been floating in space for the past year has slammed into the moon, according to scientists.

Although no-one observed the collision, a telescope in Chile spotted what astronomers have identified as a debris plume resulting from the crash.

Space tracking experts said it was inevitable that the leftover rocket segment would plough into the moon .

The school-bus-sized object is the second stage ‌of a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket that had launched a lunar lander from Firefly Aerospace toward the moon in January 2025.

Weighing 4,000kg, the rocket piece had been due to hit the moon at around 4.35pm AEST on Wednesday, travelling at around 8,690km/h.

It's the latest instance of lunar litter — rubbish left behind on the moon — that some experts believe could become a greater concern as the United States and China race to put astronauts on the moon .

In 2022, a Chinese rocket unintentionally hit the moon following a lunar mission, and more stray rocket pieces could have struck the moon in past decades without scientists' knowledge.

Julianna Scheiman, director of Dragon Human Spaceflight at SpaceX, said the company is working with NASA to avoid future wrecks.

She also emphasised that the projected crash was not deliberate. A combination of solar activity and gravity accidentally put it on a collision course with the moon, according to Scheiman.

Carl Schmidt, a planetary scientist at Boston University, said he is "100 per cent certain" that his team's observations revealed signs of the lunar crash.

The European Southern Observatory's Very Large Telescope also detected a stream of sodium and lithium stretching for tens of kilometres into space for at least five to 10 minutes following the impact, Schmidt added.

"We don't have images of the impact", but there is telescope evidence, Schmidt said in email correspondence shared with media.

Even before signs of the debris plume were spotted by the telescope in Chile, retired astrophysicist Jonathan McDowell noted that observations of the dead upper stage on Tuesday night showed it heading straight for the moon.

The anticipated crash site was a dusty, barren patch near Einstein Crater on the moon's sunlit western limb — near the edge of the near and far sides, which is especially difficult to observe from Earth.

"There's no doubt in my mind" that the rocket "is now in teeny, little pieces scattered over the moon near Einstein Crater", McDowell said.

Stargazers knew it would be difficult , if not impossible, from the ground to see the plume of dust and rock ejected from the resulting crater, let alone the flash...
body.zh: 据科学家称，过去一年一直漂浮在太空中的 SpaceX 火箭的一块碎片撞上了月球。 尽管没有人观察到这次碰撞，但智利的一架望远镜发现了天文学家认为是碰撞产生的碎片羽流。 太空跟踪专家表示，剩余的火箭部分不可避免地会撞向月球。 这个校车大小的物体是 SpaceX Falcon 9 火箭的第二级，该火箭于 2025 年 1 月从 Firefly Aerospace 向月球发射了月球着陆器。 这枚重 4,000 公斤的火箭原定于周三下午 4.35 左右（澳大利亚东部标准时间）撞击月球，飞行速度约为 8,690 公里/小时。 您值得信赖的来源，让您了解周围世界的最新动态。直接将免费的每日新闻更新和分析发送到您的收件箱。 这是月球垃圾（留在月球上的垃圾）的最新实例，一些专家认为，随着美国和中国竞相将宇航员送上月球，这可能会成为一个更大的问题。 2022 年，一枚中国火箭在完成探月任务后无意中撞上了月球，而在过去的几十年里，更多的火箭碎片可能在科学家不知情的情况下撞上了月球。 SpaceX 龙人航天项目主管朱莉安娜·谢曼 (Julianna Scheiman) 表示，该公司正在与 NASA 合作，以避免未来发生残骸。 她还强调，预计的坠机事故并非故意。谢曼表示，太阳活动和重力的结合意外地使其与月球发生了碰撞。 波士顿大学行星科学家卡尔·施密特表示，他“百分百确定”他的团队的观察揭示了月球坠毁的迹象。 施密特补充说，欧洲南方天文台的甚大望远镜还探测到，在撞击发生后，钠和锂的流向太空延伸了数十公里，持续了至少五到十分钟。 施密特在与媒体分享的电子邮件中表示，“我们没有撞击的图像”，但有望远镜证据。 甚至在智利的望远镜发现碎片羽流的迹象之前，退休天体物理学家乔纳森·麦克道尔就指出，周二晚上对死亡的上级的观测表明它直奔月球。 预期的坠机地点是月球阳光照射下的西翼爱因斯坦陨石坑附近一片尘土飞扬、贫瘠的地方——靠近近侧和远侧的边缘，从地球上观测到这一点尤其困难。 麦克道尔说，“在我看来，毫无疑问”火箭“现在已经变成了微小的碎片，散落在月球上靠近爱因斯坦陨石坑的地方”。 观星者知道，从地面上看到从形成的陨石坑中喷出的尘埃和岩石羽流，即使不是不可能，也是很困难的，更不用说闪光了……

title.en: From petitions to memes: How students made dissent visible
title.zh: 从请愿到网络迷因：学生如何让异议显现

summary.en: Student movements throughout history, from imperial China to modern India, have consistently found new ways to express dissent and challenge established authority, adapting their methods to contemporary tools and symbols.
summary.zh: 从中国古代到当今印度，学生运动不断调整其工具和象征，以挑战权威，使异议得以显现。

body.en:
From imperial China to present-day India, student movements have repeatedly adapted the tools and symbols of their age to challenge authority.

On July 22, 2026, in rainy Mumbai, India , a casually dressed young woman stepped in front of a slow-moving police van carrying detained students. She placed her palm on the hood, forcing the vehicle to stop.

Mobile phones captured the moment from every angle. She too, raised her own phone and recorded the encounter. Within hours, the clip spread across India and beyond.

It became one of the defining visuals of the Cockroach Janta Party protests, a movement in which students demanded transparency and accountability, following leaks in India's medical entrance exams.

But the power of the moment lay not only in what she did, but in how quickly it was seen. A single gesture, a young woman confronting authority , became a symbol shared across millions of screens.

While the clip belongs to a generation raised on social media, the impulse behind it is much older.

From court petitions and revolutionary posters to photographs, umbrellas and memes, student movements have repeatedly adapted the tools and symbols available to them, turning them into vehicles for dissent.

Long before television or social media carried dissent across borders, students still found ways to make their grievances heard.

In Eastern Han China, for instance, scholars at the Imperial Academy (Taixue) aligned with reform-minded officials in opposing powerful eunuchs at court, whom many viewed as corrupt and politically overbearing.

They voiced their objections through public criticism, political networks and petitions.

In an era when political communication moved through official channels, petitions were among the established ways of bringing grievances before the throne. Written in formal language and delivered through the bureaucracy, they carried student concerns directly into the state's communication system.

In Paris in 1968, students challenged university authorities and a conservative postwar social order. As demonstrations spread across the French capital and drew in workers, one of the movement's most enduring contributions emerged from a basement workshop at the Ecole des Beaux-Arts.

The Atelier Populaire ("People's Workshop") printed thousands of posters during the protests, many of them overnight. Their bold graphics, silhouettes and slogans became the visual language of the movement. Produced collectively, many carried no individual author's name, helping transform protest into a shared public voice.

The posters and their messages could appear in dozens of places overnight, giving the protest a wide local visual presence.

Protests also became more impactful when images could be transmitted across borders.

summary.en: Raising compulsory super could do the same job as raising interest rates — but the money is yours. So why aren't we talking about it?

body.en:

Every time the Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) meets to discuss the cash rate, millions of Australians hold their breath, knowing the outcome could affect their mortgage repayments , savings and household budgets.

Some economists say there's another way to cool spending — one that builds your retirement savings instead of handing more money to the bank through higher interest rates.

The Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) is due to hand down its next cash rate decision on Tuesday. Financial markets and most economists expect the RBA to leave the cash rate unchanged as inflation continues to ease, although the board has indicated it remains focused on returning inflation to its 2 to 3 per cent target.

Cooling inflation means squeezing demand somewhere. While governments can also influence demand through fiscal policy, such as changing taxes or government spending, it's now largely the RBA's job to adjust the cash rate to make borrowing more expensive. Higher interest rates can also strengthen the Australian dollar , making imports cheaper and reducing the demand for exports.

But this design hits homeowners in Australia harder than it does in many other countries, economist Chris Richardson says.

"Because we haven't built enough homes, Australia has really high housing prices and a lot of debt around that. And our interest rates are tied to short-term interest rates. So when we fight inflation, it tends to fall more on the shoulders of mortgage holders than you see in most other nations," he tells SBS News.

Richardson believes there's another lever that could be used instead of or alongside the cash rate: superannuation. Lift compulsory super contributions temporarily, and households would have less money to spend, helping cool demand, he says.

The difference is where the money goes — not interest to a bank, but savings for your own retirement.

Supporters say it could spread the burden of fighting inflation beyond borrowers. Critics argue it would simply shift the costs elsewhere. Here's how the idea stacks up.

The super guarantee (SG) is the compulsory minimum share of wages employers pay into eligible workers' superannuation. It's climbed steadily for over a decade — from 9 per cent in 2014 to its legislated final rate of 12 per cent on 1 July 2025 — with the aim of giving Australians a more comfortable retirement.

body.en:
In 2021, more than 25 million Australians shared information about their personal lives, families, and occupations as part of the Census of Population and Housing .

Data collected by the Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) painted a detailed picture of the nation's diversity.

Almost half of all Australians had a parent born overseas, and more than 400 languages were spoken , including over 180 Indigenous languages.

On Tuesday 11 August, people will again be asked to share information about their lives for the 2026 Census.

The questionnaire is compulsory for everyone in Australia on Census night, including international visitors, refugees and migrants.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

Here are some of the most common Census myths and questions — and what experts say about them.

Emily Walter, a Census national spokesperson at the ABS, said there are misconceptions that the Census is a test or graded assessment tool.

"This is a self-reported questionnaire ... so, the right answer is always what represents you the best and who you are," she told SBS Examines.

The more honestly people answered, the more accurately the data reflected Australia's population, she added.

"It's really important that we understand how our cultural makeup is changing and everyone's individual responses contribute to that ... [and] provides the opportunity for local services to be provided."

Information collected during the Census cannot be shared with police, immigration agents or any other government departments.

By law, personal information, including names and addresses, must be separated from other Census data.

After the Census, names can be retained for up to 18 months, and addresses for up to 36 months.

The ABS has spent years assessing the privacy, security and processing of its data, with all information collected during the Census protected under the Census and Statistics Act.

The Census is often referred to as a national headcount or a snapshot of the nation, but it's used to inform funding for essential services like schools, hospitals, libraries and public transportation.

Walter said people's responses influenced the location and availability of English classes for newly settled migrants, which "help them then build their language skills and support them through applying for jobs or driver's licences or all of the things that you need to support yourself".

She added that Census responses cannot be used to make a person attend English language classes.

What do extreme sports, doomscrolling, addiction, Parkinson's disease, and ADHD all have in common? Dopamine. This crucial neurotransmitter helps facilitate reward, motivation, memory and movement within the body, but are its effects always beneficial? Watch Insight episode Chasing Dopamine Tuesday 11 August 8.30pm on SBS or SBS On Demand.

When Glenn Peterson started on a higher dosage of medication to treat his Parkinson's disease symptoms, he didn't expect the consequences it would have.

"I'd see a horse race, and I'd want the thrill of it winning, and betting on it. I had constant thoughts of sex as well, which never entered my mind prior to that. I couldn't get rid of it."

The 73-year-old was diagnosed with Parkinson’s disease eight years ago. He was taking a dopamine precursor medication — a drug the body converts to dopamine when it reaches the brain — to treat his symptoms. He was later prescribed a dopamine agonist as well to make treatment more effective.

While the brain converts dopamine precursors directly into dopamine, dopamine-agonist medications mimic dopamine by activating dopamine receptors in the brain.

When combined, these drugs help treat the motor symptoms of Parkinson's, a progressive brain disorder that damages dopamine-producing neurons, but research shows agonist drugs can cause the development of compulsive and addictive behaviours.

Glenn says when the dopamine-agonist medication was increased, he developed these behaviours.

Glenn's wife, Robyn, also noticed the change when he started getting up in the middle of the night for hours at a time.

"And it started to come out that he was playing games ... or he'd gamble on the poker machines on his iPad through the night or go onto porn sites."

Glenn couldn’t understand why his mind seemed to turn against him. But when he revealed the extent of his newly developed compulsive behaviours to Robyn, she remembered the doctors had warned them that taking dopamine-agonist medication could bring on these side-effects.

They spoke to Glenn's neurologist and decreased his dose, which put an end to the compulsive behaviours.

Dopamine is a neurotransmitter in the brain that is involved in several of the body's functions, including movement — and contributes to our motivation and reward systems.

title.en: Why economists expect the Reserve Bank to hold the cash rate this week

summary.en: A recent unexpected drop in inflation has led to optimism that the Reserve Bank will maintain the current cash rate, offering potential relief after several challenging months for the economy.
summary.zh: 近期通胀意外下降，提振了人们对储备银行将维持当前现金利率的希望，这可能为经历数月经济困境后带来缓解。

body.en:
Mortgage holders will likely be able to breathe a sigh of relief with the Reserve Bank largely tipped to keep interest rates on hold.

Governor Michele Bullock and the central bank's board will meet on Monday and Tuesday, with economists forecasting the cash rate to stay at 4.35 per cent.

The prediction follows a surprise fall in inflation, despite it still being well above the bank's target band of two to three per cent.

June data revealed headline inflation fell from four to 3.8 per cent for the month, the lowest levels since the start of the Iran war.

Trimmed mean inflation, the RBA's preferred measure, remained steady at 3.6 per cent.

Senior economist at NAB, Taylor Nugent, said the RBA would likely fall into line with market forecasts.

"The RBA would need a push to deliver further tightening and the net of data flow since May has not given them that push," he said.

"Unemployment is a little above their forecast and underlying inflation marginally lower than feared."

Nugent said the RBA would likely monitor the impact of higher fuel prices on inflation following the removal of the federal government's fuel excise discount and oil prices spiking due to renewed volatility in the Middle East.

"NAB expects the next move (by the RBA) will ultimately be down, but inflation risks do remain elevated," he said.

HSBC chief economist Paul Bloxham said the central bank would likely take a wait-and-see approach before choosing to make a move on the cash rate.

"That being said, as inflation is still above target, we expect the central bank to continue to express concern that inflation is too high," he said.

"We see the downswing in growth being sufficient that the RBA begins to cut its cash rate in H2 2027."

Bloxham said there was still a chance, if inflation does not fall fast enough, that the RBA could still lift rates later in 2026.

"With trimmed mean inflation now having been above the mid-point of the RBA's target band for over four years, we see the board's tolerance for upside surprises or a slower-than-currently-projected return of inflation to target, as likely to be low."

Bullock will also face a parliamentary inquiry on Friday, where the bank's board will come under scrutiny.

Tuesday will also see fresh figures on business confidence released when NAB's latest monthly survey is unveiled.

Wall Street is meanwhile on the advance, with the US economy unexpectedly shedding jobs and amid dampened expectations the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates.

title.en: Planes narrowly avoid runway collision as delays continue at Sydney Airport
title.zh: 悉尼机场飞机险些在跑道相撞，延误持续

summary.en: Sydney Airport experienced significant flight delays and a near-collision on a runway, with officials attributing the issues to a shortage of Air Traffic Control staff over the weekend.
summary.zh: 悉尼机场周末因空中交通管制人员短缺，导致航班严重延误，并发生飞机险些在跑道上相撞的事件。

body.en:
Two planes have narrowly avoided collision on the tarmac at Sydney Airport, after days of significant delays.

A Jetstar Airbus A320 was entering an intersection at around 7am on Sunday morning when it suddenly braked to avoid being hit by an incoming Qatar Airways Boeing 777 — towed by a tug.

There were no passengers aboard the Qatar plane. However, the Gold Coast-bound Jetstar flight reported the injury of a staff member.

In footage uploaded to social media from inside the Jetstar plane, the pilot can be heard updating the passengers.

"With the sudden stop, we have had a situation where one of our cabin crew has been injured," they said.

The pilot told passengers that those directing the Qatar plane "didn't follow instructions".

"We were told to hold short and we were focused on crossing the runway, so only be chance at the last minute were we able to stop," they said.

The Australian Transport Safety Bureau (ATSB) issued a statement on Sunday afternoon, announcing it had opened an investigation into the incident.

The ATSB said it planned to collect data from both aircraft and air traffic control as part of its investigation. It will also seek to interview flight crew, ground staff and air traffic controllers on duty as well as any witnesses as the investigation proceeds.

It asked any witnesses who captured video footage of the incident to submit it via a witness form on its website.

The airport warned of delays for over 150 flights on Saturday, including 95 Qantas services.

Airservices Australia, which manages the airspace, introduced reduced traffic movements due to rostering issues.

"Airservices akcnowledged the ATFM [Air Traffic Flow Management] measures may cause some disruptions to airline scheduling and is working with airlines to reduce delays and the impact on passenger travel as much as possible," an Airservices Australia spokesperson told the ABC.

"Airservices is enhancing our training pipeline to add further controllers to improve roster depth and is working to address rostering issues that reduce the flexibility of our workforce."

Travellers also experienced delays on Friday — however were reassured by Airservices Australia that capacity had been restored and they anticipated "no further significant delays" going into the weekend.

body.zh: 经过几天的严重延误后，两架飞机在悉尼机场停机坪上险些相撞。 周日早上 7 点左右，一架捷星空客 A320 飞机在进入十字路口时突然刹车，以避免被拖船牵引的卡塔尔航空波音 777 飞机撞上。 卡塔尔飞机上没有乘客。然而，飞往黄金海岸的捷星航空航班报告称，一名工作人员受伤。 在捷星飞机内部上传到社交媒体的视频中，可以听到飞行员向乘客通报情况。 他们说：“由于突然停止，我们的一名机组人员受伤了。” 您值得信赖的来源，让您了解周围世界的最新动态。直接将免费的每日新闻更新和分析发送到您的收件箱。 飞行员告诉乘客，卡塔尔飞机的驾驶人员“没有遵守指示”。 他们说：“我们被告知要稍等一会儿，我们的注意力集中在穿越跑道上，所以只有在最后一刻我们才有机会停下来。” 澳大利亚运输安全局（ATSB）周日下午发表声明，宣布已对这起事件展开调查。 ATSB 表示，作为调查的一部分，计划从飞机和空中交通管制处收集数据。随着调查的进行，它还将寻求采访机组人员、地勤人员和值班空中交通管制员以及任何目击者。 它要求任何拍摄该事件视频的目击者通过其网站上的目击者表格提交该视频。 周六，机场警告超过 150 个航班出现延误，其中包括 95 个澳洲航空航班。 由于排班问题，管理该空域的澳大利亚航空服务公司减少了交通流量。 澳大利亚航空服务公司发言人告诉澳大利亚广播公司：“航空服务公司承认 ATFM（空中交通流量管理）措施可能会对航空公司的航班安排造成一些干扰，因此正在与航空公司合作，以尽可能减少延误和对乘客出行的影响。” “Airservices 正在加强我们的培训渠道，以增加更多管制员以提高名册深度，并正在努力解决降低我们员工灵活性的名册问题。” 周五，旅客也经历了延误，但澳大利亚航空服务公司向旅客保证，运力已经恢复，他们预计周末“不会再出现严重延误”。 如需了解 SBS 新闻的最新动态，请下载我们的应用程序并订阅我们的时事通讯。

reflection.en: The near-collision and ongoing delays at Sydney Airport highlight the critical importance of foresight and adequate staffing in complex systems. When prudence is lacking in anticipating needs, the consequences can be severe, impacting safety and efficiency. Yahweh calls us to wisdom, encouraging us to foresee potential dangers and take necessary precautions...
reflection.zh: 悉尼机场的险些相撞和持续延误事件，凸显了在复杂系统中预见性和充足人手的重要性。当缺乏远见来预估需求时，后果可能非常严重，影响安全和效率。雅伟呼召我们寻求智慧，鼓励我们预见潜在危险并采取必要的预防措施来保护他人。

verse.textEn: The prudent see danger and take refuge, but the simple keep going and pay the penalty.
verse.textZh: 通达人见祸藏躲；愚蒙人前往受害。
